robot: Franka Panda arm holding a brush fixed to its hand (no gripper)

frame.suite: world: z up, the robot base (panda_link0) at (-0.615, 0, 0), x away from the base, y to the robot's left
frame.base_text: the robot base frame: the arm's base link panda_link0, +X away from the base over the table and the sheets, +Y to the robot's left (where the paint or ink is), +Z up

arm.note: 7 joints (panda_joint1..7, rad); the tool is a brush fixed to the hand, so there is no gripper: the end-effector pose is the tip of the brush's soft tuft

ee.point: the tip of the brush's 15 mm soft tuft (tool frame tip)
ee.mode_text: rows dt apart: the service moves the tip target on a straight line from the previous row's target, one IK solve per 20 Hz control step, at most 0.25 m/s

notes: Paints: spec_file static.wells.wells (name, colour, radius 12 mm), in wells on a plate on the robot's left (+Y): the tip inside a well's circle and below the paint surface loads that paint (the brush starts dry; a new paint replaces the previous one). The main sheet (scored, under canvas_cam) and the practice sheet beside it (free for tests) are described in spec_file static.sheets; positions in the world are not given: find the sheets and the paint wells on the cameras (side_cam shows the brush's height above the paper). One continuous contact of the loaded tip with the main sheet is one stroke, and pressing deeper gives a wider mark (the handle touches the paper 15 mm below its surface). A stroke is best sent as one execute_trajectory space ee call: a few rows (above the start, press down, sweep along the stroke, lift), dt 0.1 to 0.5 s apart; the service moves the tip on a straight line between consecutive rows. Hold the brush vertical, tuft down (the start orientation). The arm is position-controlled at 20 Hz and lags a moving target. The episode ends only when your time is up.
